Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-30
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Ryan Carter (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Olivia Park (Redwood CSM), John Patel (NexaHealth CTO), Sarah Lopez (NexaHealth Eng Manager), Priya Nair (NexaHealth Data Eng)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be fuzzy):
Quick sync on POC onboarding progress, dev VPC access, initial benchmarks (hosted vs dedicated), and next steps to run dedicated performance trials. Discussed security/compliance asks (SOC2, KMS, audit logs) and prioritization of latency vs unit cost.

Topics: onboarding status, benchmark results review, tuning knobs (batching/quantization/KV cache), VPC & SSO access, next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Ryan: alright, hey everyone thanks for joining, uh this is the weekly poc sync for Nexa, uh quick roll call real fast
[00:06] John: hey John here, yep
[00:07] Sarah: Sarah on my end
[00:08] Priya: Priya here
[00:09] Maya: Maya from Redwood, hi all
[00:11] Olivia: Olivia joining, hello
[00:15] Ryan: cool, agenda — quick onboarding updates, share the hosted baseline numbers we ran yesterday, go over dev VPC access timing, talk about the dedicated run requests, and assign action items. anything missing?
[00:27] John: no that covers it, mostly want to make sure we can hit our latency targets for user-facing triage flows and confirm data residency controls
[00:34] Maya: great, quick note on baseline, we did three runs on the hosted endpoint with your anonymized sample (thank you Priya) — median p50 latencies were about 220ms per completion token for the 512-token distribution, p95 ~420ms, costs aligned with the estimate in the deck. transcript may say "K-V cash" occasionally haha
[00:55] Priya: sounds roughly what we saw on our side during the smaller test, when you say hosted endpoint, that's the public api? any special config?
[01:03] Maya: yes hosted API default profile, with streaming off for consistent measurement. we used model variant rwd-13b-q4 and default batching. for the dedicated run we expect lower p95 if we use config tweaks — batching and kv-cache warmup help a lot.
[01:18] Sarah: do you have the benchmark spreadsheet link? can we see per-shard throughput?
[01:22] Maya: yup here's the sheet — https://drive.redwood.com/nexa/poc-benchmarks (shared). the sheet's got per-request size, concurrency, tokens out, token/sec, cost simulation. some of the labels are a bit off from the auto transcribe...
[01:34] John: I saw note about q4 quantization, any accuracy regressions? we can't drop below certain QA metrics for triage suggestions
[01:42] Maya: good call — accuracy delta with q4 was within 1.5% on your eval set for intent classification and summarization tests. we ran eval harness against your gold prompts (the "nexa-prompts-v1" sheet). we recommend running the dedicated trial with the same eval set to validate at higher throughput.
[01:56] Ryan: also want to flag routing options — if latency is the top priority we can pin the dedicated pool in your region. if cost matters we can route to lower-cost variants for non-critical traffic. the smart routing policy can fall back automatically.
[02:11] Sarah: on the dedicated pool, what are the infra requirements? we have strict VPC peering rules and cert rotators, plus KMS for keys
[02:19] Maya: for private/dedicated we support VPC peering and on-prem connectors. KMS integrations are supported, we also have HSM notes in the security pack. we need dev VPC CIDRs and a contact from your infra team to set up peering. Priya?
[02:34] Priya: yes I'll share the peering info today, need to scrub PHI first and provide sample subset. timeline — I can have that by 2026-07-01.
[02:43] John: what about audit logs, retention, and SSO? legal will want RBAC and SAML
[02:49] Olivia: we can provide audit logs at the token level on request and retention tiers as an add-on. SSO via SAML/OIDC is supported; we'll include the SSO setup doc with the security bundle.
[02:59] Ryan: perfect. quick question on the hosted baseline — were there any anomalous tail latencies we should be aware of?
[03:05] Maya: a couple spikes when the KV cache was cold; when we restarted the run without cache flush p95 dropped to ~310ms. warm cache matters a lot for interactive flows. also sequence length variance spikes tail.
[03:18] Sarah: ok so for the user triage flow (avg seq len ~220 tokens) we probably need to test a warm cache scenario
[03:24] Maya: agree — dedicated trial will do warmup phase, we'll simulate steady state and cold start to measure both.
[03:31] Priya: what about throughput — can you hit 80 req/s with 250 token outputs? that's our peak
[03:36] Maya: on dedicated yes, with concurrency we can. on hosted we'd probably need horizontal concurrency and possibly a higher tier. dedicated numbers: estimate 120 req/s for that profile at p50 ~190ms, p95 ~350ms.
[03:52] John: nice. cost delta for dedicated vs hosted? we need ballpark to compare to our ops budget
[03:58] Ryan: Olivia will share pricing scenarios but to ballpark — dedicated pilot is usually higher fixed commitment but lower unit cost at scale. we'll include a small burst buffer option if you want to avoid misses.
[04:12] Sarah: can we run a run with quantization + cache + batching enabled? to see combined effect
[04:18] Maya: yes, we'll run two permutations in the dedicated trial: (A) q4 + batching + cache warm, (B) q4 without cache warm (cold start) and (C) baseline float. compare latency, throughput, and eval metrics.
[04:30] Priya: about data residency — some PHI-inferred logs need to stay in our cloud region; can Redwood honor region pinning and isolated storage?
[04:39] Ryan: yes — for Private deployments we can do region pinning and customer-managed storage with KMS. for hosted there are region options but not fully isolated storage unless you opt for dedicated/private. we'll include specifics in the security notes.
[04:52] John: any blockers on our side? Priya said she can provide peering info by 7/1 — anything else?
[04:58] Priya: I need the dev account email list and the sample dataset format spec — what's the expected schema?
[05:05] Maya: we'll send the sample schema — it's a simple csv/jsonl with prompt, context, label fields. I'll add the spec to the shared folder: https://drive.redwood.com/nexa/poc-assets
[05:16] Olivia: and I'll drop the SOC2 & ISO artifacts and the KMS integration notes into that same folder; Ryan will follow up with a short note about HSM options.
[05:25] John: perfect. also curious about failover — if the dedicated pool flaps, can traffic be routed to hosted automatically?
[05:32] Ryan: yes that's the automatic fallback policy; we can set circuit-breaker thresholds and fallback to compatible model variants in hosted to stay online. we'll include SLOs in the pilot agreement.
[05:43] Sarah: small nit — the transcribed doc earlier swapped "Roodewood" with "Redwood" in a couple places. not a problem but might confuse stakeholders.
[05:50] Maya: haha yeah the auto transcribe gets creative — "KV cache" turned into "K-V cash" once.
[05:56] Priya: one more on security — how are request logs redacted? we don't want raw PHI going to third-party storage
[06:03] Olivia: we support request-level redaction and can configure the pipeline to strip PHI before logs leave your VPC. for Private we can keep logs on customer-managed storage.
[06:13] John: thanks, that helps. for the benchmark run — what inputs do you need from us?
[06:20] Maya: sample data (anonymized), target concurrency profile, and your acceptance eval set (gold prompts). Priya mentioned she will provide those. also an IAM contact for peering.
[06:31] Priya: yep I'll send the data + contact today and confirm the scrubbed subset by 7/1.
[06:36] Ryan: ok let's recap real quick and call out owners. Ryan to send security bundle + HSM notes. Maya to run dedicated permutes and share spreadsheet. Priya to share VPC + dataset. Olivia to send pricing and SOW. John to confirm legal review stakeholders. follow-up sync 7/8.
[06:56] John: sounds good — one last Q: any surprises you typically see in enterprise pilots we should watch for?
[07:03] Maya: often networking (peering + firewall rules) and data schema mismatch are the friction points, and also eval coverage — make sure your gold set includes edge prompts. quantization surprises are minor but do verify on your evals.
[07:17] Sarah: great, thanks everyone.
[07:19] Ryan: thanks all, we'll get the docs in the folder by EOD and follow up items on the timeline.
[07:25] Olivia: thanks team, talk soon.
[07:27] End meeting.
